title: The Other Bank of the River
subtitle: Go to the other ferry, back to the mouth of the River Tiber.

content.text: Take it easy. You can't move yet. Just stay right there and listen to the report.
Wasn't the last one the "final" report?

branch.text: Urgh …
Okay. You win.
You did it, noble savior. You turned the tide and saved the world at the last moment.
And I didn't see it coming. There. Are you satisfied? Can we get to the report now?
It's your loyal greyhound licking your wounds. She's doing whatever she can to wake you up—another metaphor, of course. I'm sure I don't need to explain it.
Just another reason not to wake up yet. The salt water will get in your eyes ...
And that'll just be embarrassing for everyone. So you just keep lying there and listen to me.
You almost drowned again, but not because you're a bad swimmer.
No, it's because you'd rather die than let that spinning wheel go.
But a spinning wheel is a spinning wheel, no matter how precious the thread it spins is—and you already have one.
What's the use in having two? You're the only spinner, after all.
And even if you tear it apart, its broken components can't be used to fix yours. Just because two things look alike doesn't mean they're interchangeable.
This is a universal truth. Not just for spinning wheels, but for animals, fathers and sons—mothers and daughters.
I need to wake up.
Just wait a moment longer. The greyhound's looking for your hat.
This is the only thing she can think to do besides first aid measures.
It's cute, isn't it? Seeing her so naive and superstitious. We should play along for a little longer.
Sure, you deserve a moment of quiet, savior.
Forget about the mess out there. Take a break.
Don't rest for too long, though. The greyhound's on her way back with your hat.
If you're not awake by the time she arrives, there's no telling what she'll do.
I'm done talking. Leave me alone.

items.text: The Other Bank of the River
Altar, Sanctuary

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: She's gone? Just like that?
As Arcana vanishes, the sanctuary rocks once again. Yet more boulders fall, their tumbling cacophony heralding death.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: "The end is nigh" ...

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper, we may have slowed down the "Flood," but the water is still rising.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: There are very few options left for us now.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: This place could collapse any minute. W-We should go. We should go right now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You're right. Go find the Foundation troops. They'll get you to safety.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Wh-What about you?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I cannot allow Manus Vindictae to wipe this world clean.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The sanctuary should hold a little longer. I have to try again to stop this "Flood."

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. Ulrich risked his life to buy us this time. We mustn't squander it.
Sonetto nods, still lost in thought.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: But, neither attacking Animus nor destroying the sanctuary stopped the ritual.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What else can we do?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Even though Arcana is gone, the ritual is still ongoing. She must have left the source of its power here in the sanctuary.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They needed Dr. Dores to start the ritual. Perhaps the power source is tied to her somehow.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I need to check the altar again.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But ... But it's under the "Flood." You can't touch the water, or you'll disappear. Let me take you. I can fly you over the top, and you can take a look from there, ugh!
Nautika raises her forepaws, but her wings fail to spread. Blackened, bruised, and wounded.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll be fine, Nautika. The water can't harm me.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The "Flood" is a mix of glacier water and "Storm" water, which doesn't affect me.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So, to me, it's just ordinary water.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Look.
Water slips through her fingertips, and the hand submerged in it remains unscathed—time has left no trace.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: See? I'm fine. It's a little chilly, but nothing more.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, please take my suitcase and go with Nautika. I'll catch up to you later.
She turns around, searching for a suitable spot to enter the water. The icy water sending shivers up her thigh all the way to her neck.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper.
Behind her, Sonetto clutches the suitcase, holding off her desire to speak.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sonetto, it's dangerous here.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm your assistant. It's my duty to stay by your side, no matter how great the danger.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I'm staying. I'll wait here for your return, Timekeeper.
Leaping in, ancient bones and debris glide past.
The path forward is already decided.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: If I remember correctly, the ritual began right after Dr. Dores spun the Wheel.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: The threads ... They were drawn away somewhere deep below me. This—this isn't right.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: And the Wheel ... I can't seem to stop it.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Vertin, you must leave.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The ritual began when Dr. Dores turned the Spinning Wheel, and once it started, it kept turning as if it were sustaining the ritual.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So the Wheel must be the key to all this. That's what I should be looking for.
Just like before, with eyes closed, instinct takes over.
Upon reopening them, the golden thread flickers into view once more.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A thread?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is Dr. Dores guiding me?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's leading me deeper.
Yet it stretches without end.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ugh!
A strong current pulls a dense thicket of obscuring debris into her path; the guiding thread vanishes from just beyond her grasp.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The current is growing stronger. Regulus's song must be coming to an end.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Time's running out. I need to find the Wheel as soon as—Huh? Where did the thread go?
A familiar hum drifts from above. Clinging to the rocks, she lifts her head, and there stands the one she sought.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Dr. Dores!

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Vertin. You came. My instincts were correct. I knew you'd find your way here.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: The threads are no longer under my control. It's as if they're flowing down into some sort of well. I believe it is the source of the "Flood," too.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: If we're to have any hope of stopping this, I think we'll have to halt the Spinning Wheel first.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Agreed. Stay where you are, Dr. Dores. I'll—
A singular fixed detail catches her eye.
Dores's feet are gone, as though they never existed in the first place. She now maintains her balance by gripping the sides of the Spinning Wheel.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What happened to your feet?

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Ah. They were gone when I woke up. They must've touched the water when I was unconscious.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: My apologies. I would bring the Spinning Wheel to you, but my body will dissolve in the water.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No problem. I'll come to you.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Be careful. The current is strong here. I tried several times to escape, but the conditions are too unpredictable.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: I think it's because this is ...
A shriek cuts her off. The "Flood" churns below them.
White waves spiral, coalescing into a fathomless vortex.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Eye of the "Storm."

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Careful, Vertin. The Spinning Wheel is resuming its pace.
Dores cradles the Wheel. Its rotations seem to match the trembles of the current's pulse.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Stay right there, Dr. Dores. I'm com—Urgh!
She lets go of the rock wall and tries to move forward, but the raging waves grab her and sweep her away. Despite a moment of panic, she manages to steady herself on another rock.
A sharp slice coats her palm in red. Fortunately, the water's icy chill numbs the pain.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *coughing*
Her blood dissolves quickly in the water. Next to them, the whirlpool is growing ever larger.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *panting*

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's alright. Just try again.
Another attempt. Then three. Four ... Each time, the waves slam her back against the rock.
And the current grows fiercer.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Vertin!
Resolute, she tears her dress's hem, lashing the Spinning Wheel to her body.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Wait there. I'm bringing the Wheel to you.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Dr. Dores, no!
Propped against the rocks, Dores drags herself into the torrent. The cold wracks her with shivers, but she moves undeterred.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Ugh!
Soon, half-submerged, only her arms cling to the shore as the flood devours her lower half.
The raging pool batters her slender frame, yet she and the Spinning Wheel keep bobbing up amid the waves.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Just a little closer.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's far enough. Just stop right there, please. Don't—

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Lazo   Lock!
An unusually successful arcane skill anchors her to the rock, defying the pull of the rushing water.
She leans, stretches—yet those final meters feel insurmountable.
The Wheel shudders ever more violently now.
The roar of water fills her ears.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Vertin.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Don't worry about me.
Dores's voice cuts through the roaring waves—calm, gentle.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: I'm glad to have seen you again, child.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: I wish you my very best on the journey ahead.
Dores releases the rock. The current seizes her, pulling her forward.
The Spinning Wheel bobs on the surface while what's left of her dissolves piece by piece.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Okay. I got the Wheel.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Now take my hand, please.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Goodbye.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: DR. DORES!
And the Spinning Wheel stills, and the furious waters grow quiet.
One raindrop rises from the "Flood."
Then two, three ...
The "Flood" recedes.
And the "Storm" begins.
TO BE CONTINUED…
